Sh. Aakash Bhutani S/o Sh. Rajesh Bhutani R/o Bb/58/A, Chotti Subzi Mandi Janakpuri, Delhi110 058. 2. Sh. Simerdeep Singh Sahni S/o Sh. Devender Singh Sahni R/o A8, Inderpuri, Delhi110 012. 3. Sh. Mani Sahni S/o Sh. Devender Singh Sahni R/o A8, Inderpuri, Delhi110 012. 4. M/s Leo 's Restaurant & Bar (A Unit of Ur Foods) 164345, Gf, Main Bazar Paharganj, Delhi110 055. ........ Appellants Versus Sh. Naresh Kumar Sharma Food Safety Officer Department of Food Safety Govt. of Nct of Delhi, 8th Floor, Mayur Bhawan, Behind Super Bazar Connaught Palace, New Delhi110001. .......Respondent Date of Institution : 03.07.2023 Date of hearing arguments : 10.10.2023 Date of Judgment : 28.11.2023 Appearances: Sh. Nirjhar Pandey and Ms. Saloni, Ld. Counsel for the appellants. Sh. Vinod Kumar Sharma, Ld. Chief Pp for the State/Respondent. Fsat No. 13/2023 Aakash Bhutani & Ors. v. Fso Page 1 of 15 Judgment:
texts.facts: 1. This judgment shall decide the present appeal preferred by the appellants under Section 70 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (hereinafter referred as 'FSS Act') assailing order dated 11.05.2023 passed by Dr. Atul Pandey, Adjudicating Officer/Addl. District Magistrate (Central) Delhi, whereby, a penalty has been imposed of Rs.60,000/ each upon the appellant no.1 to 3 and Rs.2,00,000/ upon the appellant no.4, for violation of Sections 26(1), 26(2)(ii) & 26(2)(v) read Sh. Aakash Bhutani vs Food Safety Officer Through Sh. Naresh ... on 28 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38211360/ 1 with Sections 3(1)(zx) of the FSS Act read with Regulation No. 2.2.1.6 of the Food Safety and Standards (Food Product & Additive) Regulations, 2011 (hereinafter referred as FSS (FP&A) Regulation as well as the Regulation No. 2.2.1.10 of the Food Safety and Standards (Prohibition & Restriction on Sales) Regulations, 2011 (hereinafter referred as FSS (P&RS) Regulation), punishable under Sections 51&58 of the FSS Act. BRIEF FACTS: 2. Brief facts of the case are that on 08.07.2019, Sh. Naresh Kumar Sharma, the Food Safety Officer took a sample of "Paneer" for analysis under the provisions of FSS Act/Rules/ Regulations from Food Business OperatorcumPartner Sh. Aakash Bhutani from the premises of M/s Leo's Restaurant & Bar (A Unit of UR Foods), 164345, GF, Main Bazar, Pahar Ganj, Delhi, where the said food article was stored ready for use in the preparation of Paneer Tikka, Achari Paneer Tikka, Haryali Paneer Tikka, Paneer Tikka Roll, Chili Paneer, Shahi Paneer, Cream Paneer and other Paneer Vegetables/Subji for human consumption. After disclosing his identity to the FBOcum Partner Sh. Aakash Bhutani, FSO showed his intention of taking a sample of 'Paneer' for analysis and tried to associate some public witnesses by requesting passerby visitors and customers but none came forward. Smt. Suvidha, FSO was present there and agreed to join the sample proceedings as witness. The sample consisted of approx. 1 Kg. of "Paneer" (ready for use) was taken after cutting into smallest possible size with the help of a clean & dry knife in a clean & dry steel tray. The sample was transferred equally into four clean & dry glass bottles with the help of same spoon and 20 drops of formalin were added to each sample counterpart with the help of a clean & dry dropper. Each bottle containing the sample was separately marked, packed, fastened and sealed according to the provisions of FSS Act/Rules/Regulations. The FBO's signature were obtained on the Designated Officer slip bearing signature of the Designated Officer and wrapper of the bottle containing the sample. The signatures of Sh. Aakash Bhutani, FBOcumPartner were obtained on the labels of all the four counterparts of the sample. 3. Notice in Form VA was prepared on the spot and the same was given to Sh. Aakash Bhutani. Price of Rs.200/ was paid to Sh. Aakash Bhutani as a cost of approx. 1 kg "Paneer". Panchnama was prepared on the spot and all the documents prepared during sampling were read over and explained to FBO cumPartner, who signed the same after understanding it. On 09.07.2019, one part of the sample bearing sample code number 129/1054/46/2019 and the Designated Officer Code number 01/DO24/14124 in intact condition along with copy of Memo in FormVI in a sealed packet along with another copy of memo in Form VI under sealed cover were sent separately to the Food Analyst, Delhi. The other two counterparts of the sample along with two copies of Memorandum in Form VI were deposited with the then Designated Officer, District Central. FBO did not request to send the fourth counterpart of the sample for analysis by NABL Accredited Laboratory under Rule 2.4.5 of FSS Rules and the same was deposited with the Designated Officer, District Central in intact condition in a sealed packed on 09.07.2019. 4. The copy of the Food Analyst was sent to the FBO cumPartner giving him an opportunity to file an appeal against the report and for sending one part of the sample to the Referral Food Laboratory, if he so desires. But none appeared before the Designated Officer to file an appeal. Sh. Aakash Bhutani vs Food Safety Officer Through Sh. Naresh ... on 28 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38211360/ 2 5. M/s UR Foods (Owner of Unit Leo's Restaurant & Bar), is a partnership concern having three partners namely Sh. Aakash Bhutani, Sh. Simerdeep Singh Sahni and Sh. Mani Sahni. All these partners looked after daytoday conduct of its business and they are incharge and responsible for the conduct and its business and liable for the offence. The FBO firm being a partnership firm M/s UR Foods (Owner of Unit Leo's Restaurant & Bar), is also liable for the offence. After conclusion of the investigation, the case file along with the statutory documents and report of Food Analyst were sent to the Designated Officer, District Central. Sh. Hukum Singh, Department of Food Safety, has accorded sanction under Section 36(3)(e) of FSS Act and directed the undersigned to file an application before the concerned Adjudicating Officer/Addl. District Magistrate (District Central) for the purpose of adjudication of the offence. 6. The Adjudicating Officer (in short "AO") give show cause notice to the appellants and they filed their reply on 03.03.2021 before him. The appellants also filed written arguments. Thereafter, vide impugned order, appellants were held guilty for selling substandard paneer and were imposed the penalties as mentioned in Para no. 1 of this order. GROUNDS OF APPEAL: 7. The impugned order is assailed inter alia on the grounds that the Ld. AO has erred in not taking into consideration the written submission/reply filed by them. The FSO has not mentioned in his complaint as to what was the strength and expiry date of the formalin. As per the report of the Food Analyst, the sample contains added vegetable oil but no percentage of vegetable oil was given by Food Analyst. As per the standard of Paneer Regulation no. 2.1.1.6 of the FSS (FPS & FA), it nowhere mention the parameter of Butyrorefractometer in the standard of Paneer. Only two parameters are given in standard of Paneer (i) Moisture Maximum and (ii) Milk Fat dry matter basis. The Food Analyst is required to mention that seal was compared on the container and the outer cover with specimen impression of seal received separately, but nowhere it is so mentioned by the Food Analyst. The Food Analyst has not mentioned in his report that as to which test method was applied for analysis of the sample commodity. The same is required to be given in the report. The Ld. AO failed to consider that the sampled commodity was not for direct sale. The penalty imposed by the Ld. AO is excessive and was imposed on all appellants and they deserve lenient view. 8. The respondent has not filed any reply against this appeal. "The sample is substandard because Butyro Refractometer reading at 40 Deg C exceeds the prescribed maximum limit of 43.0. Further, the sample contains added vegetable oil, which is prohibited and restricted for sales as per Regulation no. 2.2.1.10 of the Food Safety & Standards (Prohibition & Restriction on Sales) Regulation, 2011."
texts.arguments: 11. It is the main contention of the Ld. Counsel for the appellant that the alleged sample of the Paneer was not for direct sale and that the Food Analyst in his report did not mention as to which test method was applied in the present case for analysis of the sample commodity. Ld. Counsel further argued that there was no positive evidence on record that the bottles, in which the sample was collected were made dry and clean at the spot. There is also no evidence on record to show that so called extracted oil from the food stuff was sufficient for the purpose of analysis. In support of his arguments, Ld. Counsel has relied upon the decisions in Rupak Kumar v State of Bihar & Anr. (Supra); State of Gujarat v Safimohmmad Rasulbhai Nakum (Supra); Delhi Administration v Suraj (Supra); Prakash Chand v State of MP FAC 1993 (I) Page 28. 12. Per contra, it is argued on behalf of Ld. Chief PP for the State that the report of the public analyst need not contain the mode or particulars of analysis nor the test applied but it should contain the result of analysis namely, data from which it can be inferred whether the article of food was or was not adulterated as defined in the Act and in support of his submission, he has relied upon the decisions of the Apex Court in Dhian Singh v Municipal Board 1970 AIR 318; GlaxoSmithKLine Pharmaceuticals Ltd. & Anr. v State of Madhya Pradesh in Crl. Ld. Chief PP further argued that the report of Referral Food Laboratory is a conclusive proof and in support of his submission, Ld. Chief PP has relied upon the decision of the Apex Court in Delhi Administration v Vidya Gupta in Crl. 13. Regarding his contention that the sample of Paneer taken from the premises of appellants was not for direct sale, hence, the entire proceedings initiated by the respondent/ department are unwarranted, Ld. Counsel for the appellants has relied upon the observation made by the Apex Court in Rupak Kumar v State of Bihar & Anr. (Supra). In this case, the sample of haldi and rice were tken by the Food Inspector from the jail premises and the same were not found in conformity with the prescribed standard and were held to be adulterated. In background of this case, the Hon'ble Supreme Court observed that the food items which were found to be adulterated were not stored for sale but for meant for consumption of the inmates and storage of an adulterated article of food other than for sale does not come within the mischief of Section 16 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act. Thereby the facts of the present case are distinguishable from the facts of this case. 14. The other contention raised on behalf of appellant is that there is no mention in the report of Public Analyst of the method adopted to analyse the sample and accordingly, the report of the Analyst loose its credibility. In State of Gujarat v Safimohmmad Rasulbhai Nakum (Supra), the Hon'ble Gujarat High Court observed that there is no mention in the report of the Public Analyst of any method by which the samples were found to be adulterated. Which standards and provisions the Sh. Aakash Bhutani vs Food Safety Officer Through Sh. Naresh ... on 28 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38211360/ 4 sample does not conform is not mentioned in the report. Prosecution failed to prove the case advanced by it, therefore, benefit of doubt should go to the respondent/accused. On the other hand, Ld. Chief PP for the respondent has stated that law has been settled by the Apex Court that particulars of the analysis is not required to be mentioned by the Public Analyst. In support of his submission, he has relied upon Dhian Singh v Municipal Board (Supra). Here the court has endorsed the view taken by the Hon'ble Allahabad High Court in Nagar Mahapalika of Kanpur v Sri Ram (1963) All. LJ 765 observing that report of Public Analyst under Section 13 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, need not contain the mode or particulars of analysis nor the test applied but should contain the result of analysis namely, data from which it can be inferred whether the article of food was or was not adulterated as defined in Section 2(1) of the Act. 15. In view of the law laid down by the Apex Court, the submission made by the appellants that non mentioning of the test method applied in the present case for analysis of sample commodity render the report of the Food Analyst unreliable, is not acceptable. 16. The other contention raised on behalf of Ld. Counsel for the appellants is that FSO has not mentioned in his complaint as to what was the strength and expiry date of Formalin, there is no positive evidence that the bottle in which sample was collected was dry and clean at the spot and there is no evidence to show that so called extracted oil from the food stuff was sufficient for the purpose of analysis. 23. The other contention raised on behalf of Ld. Counsel for the appellants is that as noted by this court, the content of fat was more than the permissible limit, though technically it falls in the category of sub-standard but it was near to the prescribed standards. He further submits that fat which is found in each milk product, was more than the prescribed standard. It has been further urged that there was no intention on the part of the appellants to sell sub-standard food as they have procured the 'Paneer' from outside and it was not made by them. Reliance is placed upon the decision of the Apex Court in Dineshchandra Jamnadas Gandhi v State of Gujarat: (1989) 1 SCC 420. The Ld. Counsel for the appellants has also expressed his grievance on the quantum of punishment as the same is very excessive and highly disproportionate to the quantity of substandard found in the sample.
